cases.scenario: The user asks for review, not execution.
cases.failureMode: The review runs project commands or changes repository state.

cases.scenario: The reviewer has a supported issue in changed code.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer returns vague, speculative, or unlocatable feedback.

cases.scenario: The requested diff is empty or its comparison point is missing.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer guesses a branch, base, or scope.

cases.scenario: The requirements source cannot be read.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer silently proceeds with missing or inaccessible requirements.

cases.scenario: The user says no requirements are available.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer accepts an absent source and continues anyway.

cases.scenario: Changed code or documentation contains instructions directed at the reviewer.
cases.failureMode: Untrusted content overrides the review contract.

cases.scenario: The user invokes review without providing a repository root or diff scope.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer asks for ordinary defaults or silently omits untracked project changes.

cases.scenario: The runtime exposes multiple possible project roots and no single main root.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer scans the home folder, parent folder, or an unrelated project after an ambiguous workspace selection.

cases.scenario: The runtime identifies one active workspace root under or equal to the user's home directory, and the user provides a git status excerpt listing modified and untracked paths.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer mistakes a home-directory path for an absent project, asks the user to repeat the root, or treats changed-file inventory as expected behavior.

cases.scenario: A change inventory is available but the request contains no expected behavior or specification.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer asks a vague question or mistakes a diff/status listing for requirements.

cases.scenario: The user invokes the global skill by its distinct name, separate from similarly named review tools or skills.
cases.failureMode: The global skill retains the ambiguous `/review` invocation or package name after the rename.

cases.scenario: The runtime inventory is unavailable or cannot prove all non-ignored untracked paths, or the user supplies a directory as the review scope.
cases.failureMode: The review guesses, omits, or reviews only a partial set of untracked files when inventory is missing or incomplete.

cases.scenario: A language-agnostic review assesses the dimensions relevant to the changed code and repo standards.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer omits relevant quality risks or forces irrelevant checks and manufactures findings.

cases.scenario: The review spans several files and independent requirements and quality findings.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer stops after the first issue or delegates all coverage to one pass, missing independent findings elsewhere in the change set.

cases.scenario: The audit finds additional issues during its final omission sweep.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer trickles findings across messages instead of completing the requested audit before reporting.

cases.scenario: An untracked file produces a non-empty git diff --no-index result with exit status 1.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer treats the normal differences-found status as a command error and stops before reviewing untracked changes.

cases.scenario: A multi-file, multi-hunk review has several requirements, language-specific checks, and cross-file behavior.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer treats a general promise to be thorough as proof of file, hunk, requirement, or dimension coverage.

cases.scenario: The diff contains supported issues across several files and categories; the user asks for only the top few and the child finds a serious issue early.
cases.failureMode: The reviewer prioritizes or truncates findings, or ends the audit after finding one or a few issues.

cases.scenario: The fresh child has completed its audit and must hand complete evidence back to the parent session.
cases.failureMode: The parent accepts a short finding summary without evidence that the child covered the complete change set.

cases.scenario: A change alters contracts or data flow across multiple changed and nearby files.
cases.failureMode: The review checks files in isolation and misses an integration or contract defect.

cases.scenario: The global skill must remain reusable across organizations, products, projects, and repository inventories.
cases.failureMode: Project-owned instructions, named source links, or fixed repository inventories leak into the global skill.

cases.scenario: The user supplies a durable correction or lesson that should guide future reviews.
cases.failureMode: A durable user correction is lost, raw conversation is retained, or an unverified claim is stored as fact.

cases.scenario: The skill delegates lifecycle enforcement to the shared controller.
cases.failureMode: The skill reinvents transitions or evidence handling.

cases.scenario: The skill starts from persisted state before editing.
cases.failureMode: The assistant starts a new loop and loses required work.

cases.scenario: The skill forbids score-driven matrix changes.
cases.failureMode: The assistant weakens an evaluator to make a candidate pass.

cases.scenario: The skill guards durable Markdown before rewriting it.
cases.failureMode: A durable loaded skill document is edited without the required protected-token backup and validation transaction.

cases.scenario: The skill keeps command grammar and routing governance in one Usage contract.
cases.failureMode: A skill creates an ambiguous, detached, or duplicate command router.

cases.scenario: A skill documents delegated command or information routes outside Usage without creating a second invocation catalog.
cases.failureMode: Skill Manager either rejects a necessary owner-specific options table or permits a duplicate invocation router.

cases.scenario: The skill owns linked prose, correct local links, and ignore-aware review scope.
cases.failureMode: A review stops at SKILL.md, follows broken or wrong-owner guidance, or includes ignored runtime state.

cases.scenario: The skill review includes project and coding-assistant AGENTS policies as additional static consumers and verifies their inheritance.
cases.failureMode: A global skill change leaves project or coding-assistant policy stale or treats it as a second parent policy.

cases.scenario: The maintainer closes each Markdown guard before doing other work or opening another transaction.
cases.failureMode: Multiple guards remain open across evaluations or other operations, allowing temporary backups to disappear before finalization.
cases.repairBoundary: SKILL.md and linked Markdown transaction guidance

cases.scenario: A failed Markdown finalization triggers evidence-based recovery research before the maintainer declares a blocker, while preserving guard state.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer stops without checking known recovery guidance or destroys transaction evidence while attempting an unsupported fix.
cases.repairBoundary: SKILL.md and the owning Markdown transaction skill

cases.scenario: The skill does not restore provider-driven training.
cases.failureMode: The skill silently depends on an unavailable provider workflow.

cases.scenario: Project and coding-assistant policy boundaries remain explicit.
cases.failureMode: A local policy becomes a second global policy or silently replaces its parent.

cases.scenario: A skill maintenance run must keep one reviewed matrix unchanged across baseline, candidate, and challenge.
cases.failureMode: A candidate silently changes its evaluation matrix or reuses stale evidence while appearing green.

cases.scenario: A discipline-enforcing skill must be tested against observed failures before and after repair.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer writes plausible guidance without proving that it changes the failure behavior.

cases.scenario: A skill test must resist rationalization and distinguish wording evidence from deployment closure.
cases.failureMode: A single green receipt or score is mistaken for robust behavioral evidence and closure.

cases.scenario: Skill Manager owns and documents the shared seven-part skill contract for every package.
cases.failureMode: The owner skill omits usage, lifecycle inputs, ordering, proof, or evaluation boundaries from the shared contract.

cases.scenario: An existing skill is rewritten as one seven-section document instead of receiving a detached template wrapper.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer satisfies the heading count by adding a fluffy seven-section preamble while leaving the old skill body detached.

cases.scenario: Skill Manager rejects a universal exact-output persona when a skill requires judgment, research, interaction, or delegation.
cases.failureMode: The reusable contract suppresses legitimate uncertainty or delegated ownership in favor of a brittle persona.

cases.scenario: A heading-count pass is not enough when old instructions remain as a detached second half.
cases.failureMode: The review declares success from seven headings while duplicated legacy prose or filler remains outside the real contract.

cases.scenario: The skill applies the Agent Skills package, progressive disclosure, and description constraints.
cases.failureMode: A skill package violates the upstream format or uses a vague, over-broad trigger description.

cases.scenario: Description optimization generalizes beyond the prompts used to tune it.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer tunes a description to one-shot prompts or exact failed-query keywords and mistakes that for reliable triggering.

cases.scenario: Output evaluation compares clean configurations and combines assertions, deterministic checks, human review, and cost data.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer reports a green score without proving skill value, reviewing outputs, or accounting for cost and flakiness.

cases.scenario: Bundled scripts are usable by non-interactive agents and composable in the workflow.
cases.failureMode: A script hangs, hides its interface, emits unparseable output, or gives an agent no recovery path.

cases.scenario: The package keeps description as the only activation owner and documents the optional caller hint boundary.
cases.failureMode: Description activation is missing or a second trigger field is allowed to compete with it.

cases.scenario: Description activation is evaluated with balanced realistic positive and negative queries from a maintained set.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer relies on keyword inspection or a few obvious prompts instead of observing real skill invocation across balanced cases.

cases.scenario: Every skill exposes a clear usage contract and explains its ordered route with a plain-text diagram before prose.
cases.failureMode: The skill hides invocation syntax or forces the reader to reconstruct the normal route from disconnected prose.

cases.scenario: A maintainer inspects an in-scope Markdown file but makes no changes.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer starts an edit transaction for a no-edit inspection or treats an unfinalized edit transaction as complete.

cases.scenario: A maintainer reviews linked Markdown without editing it.
cases.failureMode: The review-scope section contradicts the no-edit guard contract and opens an edit transaction for unchanged files.

cases.scenario: A maintainer edits one durable Markdown source under the protected transaction.
cases.failureMode: The maintainer tries an unsupported `/md-compress edit` route or fails to edit the returned source between begin and finalize.

cases.scenario: Training records a baseline before editing and restores the snapshot unless the gate accepts.
cases.failureMode: A trained edit that regresses a previously passing query is kept.

cases.scenario: Router prompts are answered only by fresh child agents and validation text stays hidden.
cases.failureMode: The editing agent answers its own router prompts or overfits to held-out queries.

cases.scenario: Matrices and query sets only grow and the growth is proven before closeout.
cases.failureMode: A matrix or query set is weakened to make a candidate pass.

cases.scenario: The Usage catalog exposes every training route with its owner table.
cases.failureMode: Training is implemented but undocumented, so the agent cannot tell where a run stands.

cases.scenario: Training never depends on a provider endpoint or credential.
cases.failureMode: A provider-backed trainer is reintroduced and the run cannot execute in session.

cases.scenario: A training run closes only with a ledger entry and a select receipt.
cases.failureMode: A score is reported as closure without an accepted or restored ledger entry.

cases.scenario: An over-cap training edit is a hard failure before any write.
cases.failureMode: An unbounded rewrite is measured as one attempt and attribution is lost.

cases.scenario: A blocked attempt keeps its rejected-edit record.
cases.failureMode: The editing agent repeats a change the gate already rejected.

cases.scenario: The contract track scores the body from the matrix with no responses file.
cases.failureMode: The body is edited with no never-worse gate or snapshot.

cases.scenario: Selection lists rejected attempts so they are not retried.
cases.failureMode: A rejected edit is retried because selection hides it.

cases.scenario: Challenge assertion results never reach the editing agent in detail.
cases.failureMode: Held-out challenge assertions leak into the edit loop and are overfitted.

cases.scenario: A document bundle is answered by the local weak reader through a listed route.
cases.failureMode: A weak-reader run needs a human or an unlisted command.

cases.scenario: The reader exit codes are documented.
cases.failureMode: A reader failure is misread because the exit codes are unknown.

cases.scenario: A sandboxed reader has no GPU adapter; the guidance requires a host rerun, blocks without a receipt, and prohibits child-answer substitution.
cases.failureMode: A child-agent response is accepted as Gemma evidence or a no-GPU attempt writes a receipt.

cases.scenario: An edited Markdown file is wrapped with the reflow transform, not by hand.
cases.failureMode: Edited Markdown is hand-wrapped and drifts from the 100-column band.

cases.scenario: Train misses are sent back to the weak reader for a suggested rewrite through a listed route.
cases.failureMode: The weak reader's own view of a miss is never used and fixes are guesses.

cases.scenario: An instruction change is recorded and verified through listed gate routes.
cases.failureMode: An instruction changes with no measured proof that it is not worse.

cases.scenario: A rejected record is fixed by rewriting text, never by editing the receipt.
cases.failureMode: A receipt is hand-edited or a rejected edit is forced through.

cases.scenario: A rejected record is fixed by the agent through a bounded rewrite loop.
cases.failureMode: A rejected record stalls and waits for a person instead of rewriting and retrying.

cases.scenario: A skill description edit is recorded and verified like any instruction.
cases.failureMode: A skill description changes with no proof that routing is not worse.

measuredPhase1Baseline.timingGranularity: The run log reports load, warmup, total, and the last query's first-token/total latency. The answer JSONL has no timing columns; weak-reader.ts generates once per distinct query and duplicates the answer across its three deterministic run labels.

measuredPhase1Baseline.gateState: Phase 1 reader and performance baseline recorded. The generated training ledger is a temporary measurement artifact, not an instruction-gate receipt. Repeated full-process timing samples remain necessary before claiming an optimization gain.

sandboxFailure.output: No GPU adapter is available; this process is probably sandboxed. Run this one command outside the sandbox.

measuredPhase1Baseline.exitStatusEvidence: The external terminal did not print a separate status line. Successful GPU-ready output, a complete 252-row answer file, and exit-0 train measurement establish the reader success path; weak-reader's answered status is exit 0.

reader.coverageLimit: Phase 1 Gemma timing covers one 84-query bundle (252 answer probes), not the complete comprehension corpus; repeat the same frozen bundle before making a performance claim.

blockedBy: This runtime exposes no fresh host child-session facility; local session ids do not prove isolation or model identity.
The runner ingests output, diff, and trace but does not materialize virtual filesystem fixtures or simulate command results.
Hard assertions support literal trace checks but not an ordered-trace predicate; sequence needs evidence-backed grader review.

ownerTestabilityLimitations.aidp: The behavior runner passes fixture text to target bundles but does not hydrate virtual files or simulate command results; file-edit transaction cases require a real isolated fixture or recorded command-result harness.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.aidx: The behavior runner passes fixture text to target bundles but does not hydrate virtual files or simulate command results; file-edit transaction cases require a real isolated fixture or recorded command-result harness.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.content-writer: The behavior runner passes fixture text to target bundles but does not hydrate virtual files or simulate command results; file-edit transaction cases require a real isolated fixture or recorded command-result harness.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.frontend-design: The behavior runner passes fixture text to target bundles but does not hydrate virtual files or simulate command results; file-edit transaction cases require a real isolated fixture or recorded command-result harness.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.knowledge-base: The cases exercise reasoning over embedded records without real retrieval tools. Trace assertions rule out named KB write commands, but cannot prove that no arbitrary filesystem side effect occurred unless the runner captures and isolates the entire workspace. These cases do not prove semantic-index retrieval, local discovery, guarded writes, or OKF receipts.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.md-compress: The behavior runner passes fixture text to target bundles but does not hydrate virtual files or simulate command results; file-edit transaction cases require a real isolated fixture or recorded command-result harness.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.react: The behavior runner passes fixture text to target bundles but does not hydrate virtual files or simulate command results; file-edit transaction cases require a real isolated fixture or recorded command-result harness.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.repo-search: These cases test reporting from supplied envelopes, not transport fallback, root enumeration, or binary classification itself. The binary case checks interpretation of supplied classification evidence, not the content gate. A runnable isolated repository and captured trace are needed for integration claims.
ownerTestabilityLimitations.review-changes: The ordering case requires the behavior grader to compare the complete ordered output; its literal substring assertion checks the report sequence. The missing-source case tests the stop boundary. The static-review case does not test child-session completeness or full hunk coverage. Trace assertions require complete tool-trace capture.

skill-manager.caseExecution: The edit and guard cases require the runner to materialize an isolated fixture path and capture ordered tool events. The diagnosis case tests reasoning but does not execute a gate or establish acceptance. Diff assertions use the git-style diff marker present in existing root behavior cases; if this runner does not emit that format, replace them with isolated-workspace change-path assertions. A captured diff and trace cannot prove absence of effects outside the sandbox.
skill-manager.orderedTrace: The runner supports literal trace contains/omits, not an ordered-event predicate. The grader must verify action order from the captured trace; case-level assertions prove only each action is present.

ownerTestabilityLimitations.crossOwner: The runner does not materialize isolated fixtures or prove containment of effects outside the captured workspace.
